sanskrit: śastrākṛtibhir ākīrṇam atīva bharatarṣabha dṛṣṭvāntarikṣam āvignāḥ pāṇḍupāñcālasṛñjayāḥ
english: Beholding the sky, O bull of the Bharatas, thickly strewn with shapes of every kind of weapon, the Pāṇḍavas, the Pāñcālas, and the Sṛñjayas were filled with dread.

sanskrit: yathā yathā hy ayudhyanta pāṇḍavānāṃ mahārathāḥ tathā tathā tad astraṃ vai vyavardhata janādhipa
english: For the more the mighty chariot-warriors of the Pāṇḍavas fought on, the more that weapon swelled in power, O lord of men.

sanskrit: vadhyamānās tathāstreṇa tena nārāyaṇena vai dahyamānānaleneva sarvato 'bhyarditā raṇe
english: Slain by that Nārāyaṇa weapon, scorched as if by fire, they were tormented on every side in the battle.

sanskrit: yathā hi śiśirāpāye dahet kakṣaṃ hutāśanaḥ tathā tad astraṃ pāṇḍūnāṃ dadāha dhvajinīṃ prabho
english: As at winter's end fire consumes the dry grass, so, O lord, that weapon consumed the host of the Pāṇḍavas.

sanskrit: āpūryamāṇenāstreṇa sainye kṣīyati cābhibho jagāma paramaṃ trāsaṃ dharmaputro yudhiṣṭhiraḥ
english: As the weapon waxed full and the army dwindled, O mighty one, Yudhiṣṭhira, the son of Dharma, fell into utmost terror.

sanskrit: dravamāṇaṃ tu tat sainyaṃ dṛṣṭvā vigatacetanam madhyasthatāṃ ca pārthasya dharmaputro 'bravīd idam
english: Seeing that army routed and bereft of sense, and Pārtha standing aloof, the son of Dharma spoke these words.

sanskrit: dhṛṣṭadyumna palāyasva saha pāñcālasenayā sātyake tvaṃ ca gacchasva vṛṣṇyandhakavṛto gṛhān
english: "Dhṛṣṭadyumna, flee with the Pāñcāla host; and you, Sātyaki, go home, surrounded by the Vṛṣṇis and Andhakas.

sanskrit: vāsudevo 'pi dharmātmā kariṣyaty ātmanaḥ kṣamam upadeṣṭuṃ samartho 'yaṃ lokasya kim utātmanaḥ
english: Vāsudeva too, righteous of soul, will do what befits himself; he who is able to counsel the whole world will surely look after his own.

sanskrit: saṃgrāmas tu na kartavyaḥ sarvasainyān bravīmi vaḥ ahaṃ hi saha sodaryaiḥ pravekṣye havyavāhanam
english: Let no battle be waged—this I say to all the troops; for I, with my brothers, shall enter the fire that bears the oblations.

sanskrit: bhīṣmadroṇārṇavaṃ tīrtvā saṃgrāmaṃ bhīrudustaram avasatsyāmy asalile sagaṇo drauṇigoṣpade
english: Having crossed the battle-ocean of Bhīṣma and Droṇa, that flood impassable to cowards, I shall be left sunk and waterless, with my host, in this cow's-hoofprint pool that is the son of Droṇa.

sanskrit: kāmaḥ saṃpadyatām asya bībhatsor āśu māṃ prati kalyāṇavṛtta ācāryo mayā yudhi nipātitaḥ
english: Let this his wish toward me, toward Bībhatsu, be swiftly fulfilled—for it was by me that the preceptor of blameless conduct was struck down in battle.

sanskrit: yena bālaḥ sa saubhadro yuddhānām aviśāradaḥ samarthair bahubhiḥ krūrair ghātito nābhipālitaḥ
english: By whose contrivance that boy, the son of Subhadrā, unskilled in warfare, was slain by many ruthless and able warriors, and went unguarded.

sanskrit: yenāvibruvatā praśnaṃ tathā kṛṣṇā sabhāṃ gatā upekṣitā saputreṇa dāsabhāvaṃ niyacchatī
english: He who, refusing to answer the question, allowed Kṛṣṇā, dragged into the assembly, to be reduced to bondage, he and his son looking on.

sanskrit: jighāṃsur dhārtarāṣṭraś ca śrānteṣv aśveṣu phalgunam kavacena tathā yukto rakṣārthaṃ saindhavasya ca
english: And that son of Dhṛtarāṣṭra, armored, eager to slay Phalguna when his horses were spent, fought to protect the Saindhava.

sanskrit: yena brahmāstraviduṣā pāñcālāḥ satyajinmukhāḥ kurvāṇā majjaye yatnaṃ samūlā vinipātitāḥ
english: He who, knowing the Brahmā weapon, struck down root and branch the Pāñcālas led by Satyajit, even as they strove to overwhelm him.

sanskrit: yena pravrājyamānāś ca rājyād vayam adharmataḥ nivāryamāṇenāsmābhir anugantuṃ tad eṣitāḥ
english: He whom, when we were unjustly driven into exile from our kingdom, we begged to follow us, yet he held us back.

sanskrit: yo 'sāv atyantam asmāsu kurvāṇaḥ sauhṛdaṃ param hatas tadarthe maraṇaṃ gamiṣyāmi sabāndhavaḥ
english: He who ever showed us the highest friendship has been slain; for his sake I shall go to my death, together with my kinsmen."

sanskrit: evaṃ bruvati kaunteye dāśārhas tvaritas tataḥ nivārya sainyaṃ bāhubhyām idaṃ vacanam abravīt
english: As the son of Kuntī spoke thus, the Dāśārha hastily stayed the army with his arms and uttered these words.

sanskrit: śīghraṃ nyasyata śastrāṇi vāhebhyaś cāvarohata eṣa yogo 'tra vihitaḥ pratighāto mahātmanā
english: "Quickly lay down your weapons and dismount from your vehicles; here is the prescribed device, the counter ordained by the great-souled one.

sanskrit: dvipāśvasyandanebhyaś ca kṣitiṃ sarve 'varohata evam etan na vo hanyād astraṃ bhūmau nirāyudhān
english: Dismount, all of you, to the ground from elephants, horses, and chariots; thus the weapon will not slay you, weaponless upon the earth.

sanskrit: yathā yathā hi yudhyante yodhā hy astrabalaṃ prati tathā tathā bhavanty ete kauravā balavattarāḥ
english: For the more the warriors fight against the power of the weapon, the stronger do these Kauravas become.

sanskrit: nikṣepsyanti ca śastrāṇi vāhanebhyo 'varuhya ye tān naitad astraṃ saṃgrāme nihaniṣyati mānavān
english: But those men who, dismounting from their vehicles, cast down their weapons—them this weapon will not slay in the battle.

sanskrit: ye tv etat pratiyotsyanti manasāpīha ke cana nihaniṣyati tān sarvān rasātalagatān api
english: Yet whoever shall withstand it, even in thought, all those it will slay, though they had gone down to the nethermost depths."

sanskrit: te vacas tasya tac chrutvā vāsudevasya bhārata īṣuḥ sarve 'stram utsraṣṭuṃ manobhiḥ karaṇena ca
english: Hearing that speech of Vāsudeva, O Bhārata, they all resolved to lay aside their weapons, in mind and in deed alike.

sanskrit: tata utsraṣṭukāmāṃs tān astrāṇy ālakṣya pāṇḍavaḥ bhīmaseno 'bravīd rājann idaṃ saṃharṣayan vacaḥ
english: Then, marking them eager to cast aside their weapons, the Pāṇḍava Bhīmasena, O king, spoke these words to rouse their spirit.

sanskrit: na kathaṃ cana śastrāṇi moktavyānīha kena cit aham āvārayiṣyāmi droṇaputrāstram āśugaiḥ
english: "By no means shall any here lay down his weapons; I will ward off the weapon of Droṇa's son with my swift arrows.

sanskrit: atha vāpy anayā gurvyā hemavigrahayā raṇe kālavad vicariṣyāmi drauṇer astraṃ viśātayan
english: Or else, with this heavy mace of golden frame, I shall range over the field like Death itself, shattering the son of Droṇa's weapon.

sanskrit: na hi me vikrame tulyaḥ kaś cid asti pumān iha yathaiva savitus tulyaṃ jyotir anyan na vidyate
english: For no man here is the equal of my valor, even as there is no other light to match the light of the Sun.

sanskrit: paśyadhvaṃ me dṛḍhau bāhū nāgarājakaropamā samarthau parvatasyāpi śaiśirasya nipātane
english: Behold these two firm arms of mine, like the trunks of a king of elephants, able to bring down even Himālaya, the snow-clad mountain.

sanskrit: nāgāyutasamaprāṇo hy aham eko nareṣv iha śakro yathā pratidvaṃdvo divi deveṣu viśrutaḥ
english: For I alone among men have the strength of ten thousand elephants, even as Śakra is renowned in heaven as the peerless rival among the gods.

sanskrit: adya paśyata me vīryaṃ bāhvoḥ pīnāṃsayor yudhi jvalamānasya dīptasya drauṇer astrasya vāraṇe
english: This day behold the prowess of my thick-shouldered arms in the fray, as I ward off the blazing, flaming weapon of Droṇa's son.

sanskrit: yadi nārāyaṇāstrasya pratiyoddhā na vidyate adyainaṃ pratiyotsyāmi paśyatsu kurupāṇḍuṣu
english: If there be none to withstand the Nārāyaṇa weapon, this day I shall withstand it before the eyes of the Kurus and the Pāṇḍavas."

sanskrit: evam uktvā tato bhīmo droṇaputram ariṃdamaḥ abhyayān meghaghoṣeṇa rathenādityavarcasā
english: Having spoken thus, Bhīma, the tamer of foes, advanced upon the son of Droṇa in his sun-bright chariot, thundering like a cloud.

sanskrit: sa enam iṣujālena laghutvāc chīghravikramaḥ nimeṣamātreṇāsādya kuntīputro 'bhyavākirat
english: Swift in his nimbleness, the son of Kuntī reached him in the twinkling of an eye and overwhelmed him with a net of arrows.

sanskrit: tato drauṇiḥ prahasyainam udāsam abhibhāṣya ca avākirat pradīptāgraiḥ śarais tair abhimantritaiḥ
english: Then the son of Droṇa, laughing and addressing him with disdain, showered upon him those consecrated arrows with blazing points.

sanskrit: pannagair iva dīptāsyair vamadbhir analaṃ raṇe avakīrṇo 'bhavat pārthaḥ sphuliṅgair iva kāñcanaiḥ
english: As though by flame-mouthed serpents vomiting fire in the battle, Pārtha was covered over, as if with golden sparks.

sanskrit: tasya rūpam abhūd rājan bhīmasenasya saṃyuge khadyotair āvṛtasyeva parvatasya dinakṣaye
english: Such, O king, was the aspect of Bhīmasena in the fray—like a mountain wrapped about with fireflies at the close of day.

sanskrit: tad astraṃ droṇaputrasya tasmin pratisamasyati avardhata mahārāja yathāgnir aniloddhataḥ
english: As that weapon of Droṇa's son met him in conflict, it grew greater, O great king, like fire fanned by the wind.

sanskrit: vivardhamānam ālakṣya tad astraṃ bhīmavikramam pāṇḍusainyam ṛte bhīmaṃ sumahad bhayam āviśat
english: Seeing that weapon of terrible power waxing ever greater, a mighty fear seized the Pāṇḍava host, save Bhīma alone.

sanskrit: tataḥ śastrāṇi te sarve samutsṛjya mahītale avārohan rathebhyaś ca hastyaśvebhyaś ca sarvaśaḥ
english: Then they all cast their weapons down upon the earth and dismounted, every one, from their chariots, elephants, and horses.

sanskrit: teṣu nikṣiptaśastreṣu vāhanebhyaś cyuteṣu ca tad astravīryaṃ vipulaṃ bhīmamūrdhany athāpatat
english: When they had laid down their weapons and quit their vehicles, the vast might of that weapon fell upon the head of Bhīma.

sanskrit: hāhākṛtāni bhūtāni pāṇḍavāś ca viśeṣataḥ bhīmasenam apaśyanta tejasā saṃvṛtaṃ tadā
english: All beings cried out in dismay, and the Pāṇḍavas above all, as they beheld Bhīmasena then enveloped in that fiery splendor.

sanskrit: saṃjaya uvāca bhīmasenaṃ samākīrṇaṃ dṛṣṭvāstreṇa dhanaṃjayaḥ tejasaḥ pratighātārthaṃ vāruṇena samāvṛṇot
english: Saṃjaya said: Seeing Bhīmasena overspread by the weapon, Dhanaṃjaya, to counter its fiery splendor, enveloped him with the Vāruṇa weapon.

sanskrit: nālakṣayata taṃ kaś cid vāruṇāstreṇa saṃvṛtam arjunasya laghutvāc ca saṃvṛtatvāc ca tejasaḥ
english: None could descry him, shrouded by the Vāruṇa weapon, by reason of Arjuna's swiftness and of the splendor that enveloped him.

sanskrit: sāśvasūtaratho bhīmo droṇaputrāstrasaṃvṛtaḥ agnāv agnir iva nyasto jvālāmālī sudurdṛśaḥ
english: Bhīma, with horses, charioteer, and car, shrouded by the weapon of Droṇa's son, garlanded in flame and scarcely to be looked upon, was like fire cast into fire.

sanskrit: yathā rātrikṣaye rājañ jyotīṃṣy astagiriṃ prati samāpetus tathā bāṇā bhīmasenarathaṃ prati
english: As at the close of night, O king, the stars sink toward the western mountain, so did the arrows converge upon the chariot of Bhīmasena.

sanskrit: sa hi bhīmo rathaś cāsya hayāḥ sūtaś ca māriṣa saṃvṛtā droṇaputreṇa pāvakāntargatābhavan
english: For Bhīma, and his chariot, his horses, and his charioteer, O sire, enveloped by Droṇa's son, seemed sunk within the very fire.

sanskrit: yathā dagdhvā jagat kṛtsnaṃ samaye sacarācaram gacched agnir vibhor āsyaṃ tathāstraṃ bhīmam āvṛṇot
english: As the fire, having burned at the appointed time the whole world with all that moves and moves not, passes into the mouth of the Almighty, so did that weapon enwrap Bhīma.

sanskrit: sūryam agniḥ praviṣṭaḥ syād yathā cāgniṃ divākaraḥ tathā praviṣṭaṃ tat tejo na prājñāyata kiṃ cana
english: As fire might enter the sun, or the sun enter fire, so that splendor entered in, and nothing whatever could be discerned.

sanskrit: vikīrṇam astraṃ tad dṛṣṭvā tathā bhīmarathaṃ prati udīryamāṇaṃ drauṇiṃ ca niṣpratidvaṃdvam āhave
english: Seeing that weapon poured forth upon Bhīma's chariot, and the son of Droṇa rising up without a rival in the battle,

sanskrit: sarvasainyāni pāṇḍūnāṃ nyastaśastrāṇy acetasaḥ yudhiṣṭhirapurogāṃś ca vimukhāṃs tān mahārathān
english: all the hosts of the Pāṇḍavas, weapons laid aside and senses fled, with Yudhiṣṭhira at their head—those mighty chariot-warriors turned their faces away.

sanskrit: arjuno vāsudevaś ca tvaramāṇau mahādyutī avaplutya rathād vīrau bhīmam ādravatāṃ tataḥ
english: Then Arjuna and Vāsudeva, those two heroes of great splendor, leaping in haste from their chariot, ran toward Bhīma.

sanskrit: tatas tad droṇaputrasya tejo 'strabalasaṃbhavam vigāhya tau subalinau māyayāviśatāṃ tadā
english: Then those two mighty ones plunged into the splendor of Droṇa's son, born of the weapon's power, and entered it by their magic art.

sanskrit: nyastaśastrau tatas tau tu nādahad astrajo 'nalaḥ vāruṇāstraprayogāc ca vīryavattvāc ca kṛṣṇayoḥ
english: They had laid aside their weapons, and so the fire born of the weapon could not burn them—both by the working of the Vāruṇa weapon and by the might of the two Kṛṣṇas.

sanskrit: tataś cakṛṣatur bhīmaṃ tasya sarvāyudhāni ca nārāyaṇāstraśāntyarthaṃ naranārāyaṇau balāt
english: Then Nara and Nārāyaṇa, to quell the Nārāyaṇa weapon, forcibly dragged forth Bhīma and all his weapons.

sanskrit: apakṛṣyamāṇaḥ kaunteyo nadaty eva mahārathaḥ vardhate caiva tad ghoraṃ drauṇer astraṃ sudurjayam
english: Even as he was being dragged away, the son of Kuntī, that mighty car-warrior, kept roaring on; and the dreadful, scarce-conquerable weapon of Droṇa's son kept growing.

sanskrit: tam abravīd vāsudevaḥ kim idaṃ pāṇḍunandana vāryamāṇo 'pi kaunteya yad yuddhān na nivartase
english: Vāsudeva said to him: "What is this, son of Pāṇḍu? Why, O son of Kuntī, though restrained, do you not turn back from battle?

sanskrit: yadi yuddhena jeyāḥ syur ime kauravanandanāḥ vayam apy atra yudhyema tathā ceme nararṣabhāḥ
english: Were these sons of the Kurus to be conquered by fighting, we too would fight here, and so would these bulls among men.

sanskrit: rathebhyas tv avatīrṇās tu sarva eva sma tāvakāḥ tasmāt tvam api kaunteya rathāt tūrṇam apākrama
english: But all your own people have dismounted from their chariots; therefore you too, O son of Kuntī, withdraw at once from your car."

sanskrit: evam uktvā tataḥ kṛṣṇo rathād bhūmim apātayat niḥśvasantaṃ yathā nāgaṃ krodhasaṃraktalocanam
english: Having spoken thus, Kṛṣṇa brought him down from the chariot to the ground, hissing like a serpent, his eyes red with wrath.

sanskrit: yadāpakṛṣṭaḥ sa rathān nyāsitaś cāyudhaṃ bhuvi tato nārāyaṇāstraṃ tat praśāntaṃ śatrutāpanam
english: When he had been dragged from the chariot and his weapon laid upon the ground, then that Nārāyaṇa weapon, scorcher of foes, grew still.

sanskrit: tasmin praśānte vidhinā tadā tejasi duḥsahe babhūvur vimalāḥ sarvā diśaḥ pradiśa eva ca
english: When that unbearable splendor was thus quelled by the prescribed device, all the quarters and the intermediate quarters became clear.

sanskrit: pravavuś ca śivā vātāḥ praśāntā mṛgapakṣiṇaḥ vāhanāni ca hṛṣṭāni yodhāś ca manujeśvara
english: Auspicious breezes blew, the beasts and birds grew calm, and the vehicles and the warriors were filled with cheer, O lord of men.

sanskrit: vyapoḍhe ca tato ghore tasmiṃs tejasi bhārata babhau bhīmo niśāpāye dhīmān sūrya ivoditaḥ
english: And when that terrible splendor was withdrawn, O Bhārata, the wise Bhīma shone forth like the sun risen at the close of night.

sanskrit: hataśeṣaṃ balaṃ tatra pāṇḍavānām atiṣṭhata astravyuparamād dhṛṣṭaṃ tava putrajighāṃsayā
english: There stood the remnant of the Pāṇḍavas' host that the slaughter had spared, rejoicing at the ceasing of the weapon, eager to slay your son.

sanskrit: vyavasthite bale tasminn astre pratihate tathā duryodhano mahārāja droṇaputram athābravīt
english: When that army had rallied and the weapon had been thus countered, Duryodhana, O great king, spoke to the son of Droṇa.

sanskrit: aśvatthāman punaḥ śīghram astram etat prayojaya vyavasthitā hi pāñcālāḥ punar eva jayaiṣiṇaḥ
english: "Aśvatthāman, loose this weapon again, and swiftly; for the Pāñcālas have rallied once more, hungry for victory."

sanskrit: aśvatthāmā tathoktas tu tava putreṇa māriṣa sudīnam abhiniḥśvasya rājānam idam abravīt
english: Aśvatthāman, thus addressed by your son, O sire, sighing most piteously, said this to the king.

sanskrit: naitad āvartate rājann astraṃ dvir nopapadyate āvartayan nihanty etat prayoktāraṃ na saṃśayaḥ
english: "This weapon does not return, O king; it cannot be employed a second time. He who would call it back, it slays him who wields it—of this there is no doubt.

sanskrit: eṣa cāstrapratīghātaṃ vāsudevaḥ prayuktavān anyathā vihitaḥ saṃkhye vadhaḥ śatror janādhipa
english: And this Vāsudeva has applied the counter to the weapon; otherwise the slaughter of the foe in battle had been ordained, O lord of men.

sanskrit: parājayo vā mṛtyur vā śreyo mṛtyur na nirjayaḥ nirjitāś cārayo hy ete śastrotsargān mṛtopamāḥ
english: Defeat or death—death is the better, not so this victory; for these foes, vanquished, are as good as dead, having cast away their weapons."

sanskrit: duryodhana uvāca ācāryaputra yady etad dvir astraṃ na prayujyate anyair gurughnā vadhyantām astrair astravidāṃ vara
english: Duryodhana said: "Son of the preceptor, if this weapon may not be loosed twice, then with other weapons let the slayers of the teacher be slain, O best of those who know the arts of war.

sanskrit: tvayi hy astrāṇi divyāni yathā syus tryambake tathā icchato na hi te mucyet kruddhasyāpi puraṃdaraḥ
english: For in you the celestial weapons abide as they do in the Three-eyed God; should you wish it in your wrath, not even Purandara could escape you."

sanskrit: dhṛtarāṣṭra uvāca tasminn astre pratihate droṇe copadhinā hate tathā duryodhanenokto drauṇiḥ kim akarot punaḥ
english: Dhṛtarāṣṭra said: When that weapon had been countered, and Droṇa slain by guile, and the son of Droṇa thus addressed by Duryodhana, what did he do next?

sanskrit: dṛṣṭvā pārthāṃś ca saṃgrāme yuddhāya samavasthitān nārāyaṇāstranirmuktāṃś carataḥ pṛtanāmukhe
english: And seeing the Pārthas arrayed for battle in the fray, freed from the Nārāyaṇa weapon, ranging at the head of the host—

sanskrit: saṃjaya uvāca jānan pituḥ sa nidhanaṃ siṃhalāṅgūlaketanaḥ sakrodho bhayam utsṛjya abhidudrāva pārṣatam
english: Saṃjaya said: He whose banner bore the lion's tail, knowing the slaying of his father, full of wrath, casting off all fear, rushed upon the son of Pṛṣata.

sanskrit: abhidrutya ca viṃśatyā kṣudrakāṇāṃ nararṣabhaḥ pañcabhiś cātivegena vivyādha puruṣarṣabham
english: And rushing on, that bull among men pierced that bull among men with twenty small arrows and with five more, in a great fury.

sanskrit: dhṛṣṭadyumnas tato rājañ jvalantam iva pāvakam droṇaputraṃ triṣaṣṭyā tu rājan vivyādha patriṇām
english: Then Dhṛṣṭadyumna, O king, pierced the son of Droṇa—blazing like fire—with sixty-three feathered shafts, O king.

sanskrit: sārathiṃ cāsya viṃśatyā svarṇapuṅkhaiḥ śilāśitaiḥ hayāṃś ca caturo 'vidhyac caturbhir niśitaiḥ śaraiḥ
english: And he pierced his charioteer with twenty gold-feathered, stone-whetted shafts, and his four horses with four sharp arrows.

sanskrit: viddhvā viddhvānadad drauṇiḥ kampayann iva medinīm ādadat sarvalokasya prāṇān iva mahāraṇe
english: Piercing and piercing again, the son of Droṇa roared, as though making the earth tremble, as though seizing the life-breaths of all the world in that great battle.
